answer: The watchers time every geyser eruption to the second and keep the intervals in a log that runs for a full year. A plume interval copied from another geyser fails the log: at the horizon of the eruption the timing must match the watchers' own clocks, and a copied interval belongs to another spring. Faking a year of timings means camping by the geyser for twelve months and paying 14,600 in wages and food, and the garden stamp on the logbook is countersigned weekly, so a geyser whose eruptions were never timed is struck from the record.
